title: Signs for Lorries: Weight, Height & Width
whatItIs: Red circles tell you what you must not do; red triangles warn. Learn the signs that restrict lorries by weight, type, width, length and height.
keyFacts: Red rings or circles tell you what you must not do.

keyFacts.text: An overheight vehicle MUST NOT pass a red-circle height restriction sign: it is unlawful.

keyFacts: A red warning triangle shows the maximum headroom under a bridge or other overhead obstruction ahead.
Bridges with under 16 ft 6 in (about 5 m) clearance are normally signed.
Plates can add exemptions, such as 'Except for loading' by goods vehicles, or access to premises.

visual.caption: Official signs that restrict or warn lorry drivers

a.label: Red circle (e.g. maximum height)
points: An order: no vehicles over the height shown

b.label: Red triangle (headroom)
points: Warns of the maximum headroom ahead
May be well before the bridge, with a distance plate

onTheTest.question: You see a red circle showing a lorry and the figure 7.5 t. What does it mean?
options: No goods vehicles over 7.5 tonnes gross weight
Lorries over 7.5 tonnes must use the left lane
Goods vehicles must keep below 7.5 mph
onTheTest.why: This regulatory sign means no goods vehicles over the maximum gross weight shown, in tonnes.

onTheTest.question: A goods vehicle weight limit sign has an 'Except for loading' plate. What does it mean?
options: Goods vehicles may enter only to load or unload
There is a loading bay ahead
The limit applies only while you are loading
onTheTest.why: The plate shows an exemption from the prohibition: 'except for loading and unloading by goods vehicles'.

traps: Red circle = an order; red triangle = a warning. Both can show a headroom figure.
'Except for loading' exempts goods vehicles only to load and unload.
At an arch bridge, a high vehicle may need the middle of the road: other drivers should give way to it.
